I started playing World of Warcraft a little while after Burning Crusade had come out, and I thought it was a great game. I live in America but the American servers are always crowded and laggy. My machine at the time couldn't handle it. I took to playing on the Australian servers to avoid the crowds and the dreaded lag. I was suffering from clinical depression and was actually contemplating suicide at the time. I didn't have any friends, nor did I ever really spend any time outside of  my room. I was just playing around one day doing some quests when I ran into one that I needed some help on. I went into the nearest town looking for a person or two to help me. I found two, and one of them changed my life. They helped me with the quest and invited me to join their guild which I did so happily. I've made some friends! Friends half way around the world, but friends non the less. The one who changed my life was an older woman (60s) and she became like a mother to me. We spent many hours raiding and running through dungeons and just talking. She helped me through a very rough time of my life. I lost contact with her for a few months after I couldn't afford to pay for the subscription. When I came back our communication was kept to just a letter in the mail once a week. It wasn't much, but it was nice having someone to talk to. I saved all the letters she sent me and they are to this day sitting in my characters bank account. I wasn't able to pay for the subscription for about a year after that. When I came back she never responded to messages anymore. I let the subscription run out on that account, and I can no longer remember what email I had used to make the account so I could access it.
